rulings.reason: The instruction does not score the presence of taboo subject matter; its operative clause asks whether that material is carrying the joke essentially alone 'with little additional wit layered on top', which forces the judge to assess wit density and construction rather than topic. A high score therefore is direct (inverse) evidence about comedic craft -- a one-trick shock pun -- and not merely a subject-matter fingerprint that travels with quality.

The instruction measures self-containedness -- whether the payoff needs an external scandal or biographical fact -- which a brilliantly executed allusive entry and an inert one would both score at the ceiling, so the score is about the entry's topical mode, not its quality. It is marked mixed because the upstream cause (building a joke on a well-chosen real-world referent) plausibly co-occurs with genuine inventiveness, so the discount could suppress real craft signal.
